previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and a history of kidney transplant rejection presented with dyspnea, cough, and nasal congestion over two days. He was treated by EMS with albuterol nebulizers for wheezing, which provided partial relief. Admission labs showed hyperkalemia with a potassium of 6.3 and a BNP of 27,000, though chest imaging revealed no acute cardiopulmonary process. He received kayexalate for potassium management and underwent hemodialysis the following day, removing 2.1 liters of fluid. His potassium improved to 5.4, and respiratory symptoms resolved with albuterol and Mucinex DM. Lisinopril was held initially but restarted before discharge. He was discharged home with an albuterol inhaler, Mucinex DM, adjusted sevelamer dosing, and home health follow-up.

In the ED, initial VS: 97.7, 100/64, 72, 12, 96% RA, ___ pain. 
Exam otherwise notable for guaiac negative stool. Labs revealed

1L normal saline. Transplant surgery was consulted, and 
recommended obtaining an abdominal plain film, which showed 
multiple air-fluid levels, but no dilated loops of bowel. Prior 
to transfer the patient's vital signs were 97.6, 100/87, 16, 94% 
RA, with zero/10 pain. He was tolerating POs in the ED.

On arrival to the floor, the patient has no complaints.

radiology_notes.text:
PA AND LATERAL CHEST ___, AT 20:56 HOURS.

HISTORY:  Epigastric pain with vomiting.  Assess for free air under the
diaphragm.

COMPARISON:  Multiple priors, the most recent dated ___.

FINDINGS:  An extensive fine reticular nodular interstitial pattern is again
identified and has been previously evaluated with x-rays and CT.  The overall
lungs are grossly stable.  Mild aortic tortuosity is again noted with
calcified plaque seen at the arch.  The cardiac silhouette is borderline
enlarged but stable.  No effusion or pneumothorax is noted.  There is no free
air under the diaphragm.  The stomach is incompletely distended with an
air-food/fluid layer.  A dextroconcave scoliosis of the thoracic spine is
again noted and stable as well.  Healed trauma of the mid diaphysis of the
left clavicle is again noted.

IMPRESSION:  No acute pulmonary process.  Chronic interstitial lung disease as
previously documented.  No free air under the diaphragm detected.

SUPINE AND UPRIGHT ABDOMEN, ___ AT 2100 HOURS.

HISTORY:  Epigastric pain.

COMPARISON:  Multiple priors, the most recent dated ___.

FINDINGS:  No dilated loops of small bowel are evident.  Innumerable air-fluid
levels are detected, most predominantly throughout the colon.  The stomach is
mildly distended with an air-fluid and fluid level.  Severe vascular
calcification is noted extending into the small vessels of the pelvis. 
Overlying osseous structures are unremarkable.  No free intraperitoneal air is
identified.

IMPRESSION:  Innumerable air-fluid levels, most likely all within the colon. 
No definite dilated loops of small bowel are evident.  If concern for
perforation or bowel pathology persists, consider CT of the abdomen and pelvis
for more sensitive evaluation.
